entries.content:
The problem: `open_dict(cfg)` only opens the root, but the struct flag on nested `cfg.hydra` is True (set separately at line 268). `OmegaConf.update` with a nested key fails since `cfg.hydra` is struct. Fix: recursively open? Actually the upstream fix (hydra commit "fix: cannot add a value to hydra.job.env_set"): In `_load_configuration`, they used `with open_dict(cfg.hydra.job.env_set)`? Actually I recall the fix: in compose_hydra_configuration or load, they set struct False on hydra job env... Let me check upstream: hydra issue #1014? The fix was PR #1027 "fixing bug where one could not add a config value to hydra.job.env_set". I believe the fix was in config_loader_impl, `_apply_overrides_to_config`: when adding, open dict recursively. But open_dict opens the root cfg which propagates? open_dict sets struct False only on that node and doesn't propagate to children? In omegaconf, set_struct on a node with struct=True set explicitly on child — open_dict only affects the node's own flag... Actually omegaconf set_struct applies recursively. open_dict sets the flag on the node only. So cfg.hydra has struct=True explicitly set (line 268), and open_dict(cfg) doesn't clear it.

Simplest fix: in is_add branch, also open cfg.hydra? Better general fix: use `OmegaConf.set_struct(cfg, False)` temporarily, which is recursive. Let me implement:

```python
elif override.is_add():
    if OmegaConf.select(cfg, key, throw_on_missing=False) is None:
        with open_dict(cfg):
            OmegaConf.update(cfg, key, value)
```

Change to temporarily set struct False recursively? But open_dict saves/restores flag only for the node. Could do:

```python
last_dot = key.rfind(".")
parent = cfg if last_dot == -1 else OmegaConf.select(cfg, key[0:last_dot])
with open_dict(parent):
    OmegaConf.update(cfg, key, value)
```

But parent may itself not have struct explicitly set; the struct is inherited from cfg.hydra? struct flags are per-node; OmegaConf checks _get_flag which walks parents. If cfg root is opened and parent (hydra.job) has no explicit flag, inherited False. But cfg.hydra had set_struct(cfg.hydra, True) which recursively sets True on all children of hydra. So hydra.job.env_set is explicitly struct=True. Opening parent = cfg.hydra.job works: open_dict saves struct of that node, sets False, update works (struct check walks up from target). Should work.

But actually the upstream fix I vaguely recall: in `_load_configuration` they wrapped `ConfigLoaderImpl._apply_overrides_to_config(config_overrides, cfg)` — and the actual fix commit: "Fixing bug in structured config + overriding". Let me just check git log in repo? Not available offline maybe. Simpler: implement the parent-open fix in is_add branch, handling the case where intermediate nodes exist. For `+hydra.job.env_set.WANDB_NOTES`, last_dot exists, parent = cfg.hydra.job.env_set — select it, open it. open_dict on DictConfig works.

Edge: `+new_group.sub` where parent `new_group` doesn't exist — OmegaConf.select returns None; then open_dict(None) fails. Handle: if parent is None, use cfg. But then intermediate creation through struct nodes? If cfg struct opened but cfg.hydra struct True, adding `+hydra.foo` would fail. Parent = cfg.hydra (exists) → fine. Only when parent doesn't exist is the intermediate struct question moot (creating new nodes under an opened cfg root is fine; cfg.hydra struct blocks only keys under hydra, which exist). So fallback to cfg is fine.

Implement and test.

entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Root cause: in `ConfigLoaderImpl._apply_overrides_to_config`, the `+` (add) branch wrapped `OmegaConf.update` in `open_dict(cfg)`, which only clears the struct flag on the root config node. However, `cfg.hydra` (and its children like `hydra.job.env_set`) had struct recursively set to `True` earlier in `_load_configuration` (line 268), so adding a key under `hydra.*` still failed with "Key 'WANDB_NOTES' is not in struct". The fix selects the actual parent node of the key being added and opens it with `open_dict(parent)` (falling back to the root when the parent doesn't exist), restoring struct mode afterwards. Verified the issue's command works (`+hydra.job.env_set.WANDB_NOTES="X"` is merged), top-level and nested adds still work, struct is restored, and the existing test suite shows no new failures (remaining failures are pre-existing on the baseline).
